scenario: [LINT.4.4] an empty interval overlaps nothing, including a non-empty one that strictly contains it. empty = (5..5) lies strictly inside wide = (0..10), which is the degenerate case: both CROSS-INTERVAL comparisons (i1.start < i2.end and i2.start < i1.end) hold, while the intersection is empty and [LINT.7.1] admits no instant in common. Pins the four-conjunct lowering at `dsc.rete`'s `lint_3_1_1_relation`, its `overlaps` arm — specifically its two NON-EMPTINESS conjuncts; dropping either one turns this vector red. Both operand orders are driven (rules `empty_inside` and `inside_empty`) because the intersection form is symmetric ([LINT.4.1]'s lint_4_1__overlaps_symmetric) and a lowering can be wrong in one direction only. The control rule `wide_other` must fire: without it a lowering that answered FALSE for every `overlaps` would pass this vector, and the negative pair would pin nothing.
rules_ds:
schema Range scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    start: Int mutable
    end: Int mutable

rule empty_inside:
    Range e where e.entity_id == "empty"
    Range w where w.entity_id == "wide" and (e.start..e.end) overlaps (w.start..w.end)
->
    log critical "empty-inside"

rule inside_empty:
    Range w2 where w2.entity_id == "wide"
    Range e2 where e2.entity_id == "empty" and (w2.start..w2.end) overlaps (e2.start..e2.end)
->
    log critical "inside-empty"

rule wide_other:
    Range x where x.entity_id == "wide"
    Range y where y.entity_id == "other" and (x.start..x.end) overlaps (y.start..y.end)
->
    log critical "wide-other"
